_comment: Tier B sources for next/developers/object-model pages: concepts with no speckle-bundle-spec-generated catalog to diff against (see the sync-object-model-docs skill). Each entry pins the sha256 of a source file as of the last time an agent actually read it and drew a conclusion from it. check-object-model-freshness.mjs re-hashes these sibling-checkout files and flags any that changed, so a stale conclusion gets re-verified instead of silently rotting. Update the hash (and the note, if the fact changed) whenever you re-verify or the source moves.

entries.concept: Server-side ingestion contract (GraphQL ingestion mutations and inputs, REST sign/complete, ETag and additionalRequestHeaders handling, LEGACY_SEND_UNSUPPORTED and BUNDLE_REFERENCE_NOT_FOUND, the projectVersionsUpdated CREATED signal, viewer .dat gating, artifacts endpoint, multipart threshold)
entries.note: Also grounds version-metadata.mdx's server-side claims. Verified 2026-09-16 against speckle-server-internal on branch jbr/fea-504-grasshopper-publish-versionmessage-is-not-shown-on-the-model with a DIRTY worktree: upload.ts and envelopeVersion.ts were hashed from the worktree and include the uncommitted `message` field on the uploads/complete body that publish.mdx documents. If the freshness check flags those two files, first check whether that change merged (hash moves but the docs stay right) or was dropped (the `message` key on the page is then wrong). Facts corrected on the pages during this pass: the version-created signal is the projectVersionsUpdated subscription (type CREATED; internal event versions.created; webhook commit_create) — there is no version_created; apollographql-client-name is never read by the server and apollographql-client-version is analytics-only, the publishing app comes from the ingestion's sourceData; the sign response may carry additionalRequestHeaders the PUT must send (always on Azure); failWithInvalid/failWithCancel have distinct input types; multipart is for files over the 5 GB single-PUT ceiling; LEGACY_SEND_UNSUPPORTED is a 422 raised when the server has no legacy-send support (isLegacySendSupported), not a named '2026.9-only' setting. Not server-enforced (spec/consumer rules only): meta.produced_by/producer_version, the 1536 MiB shard cap.

entries.concept: SGEO geometry encoding (geometries table row shape and sharding, 16-byte header, primitive codes, flag bits, body layouts, CRC and id spans, encoder/decoder names) and the viewer .dat (name, gating, layout, realizations)
entries.note: Verified 2026-09-16 across speckle-bundle-spec, speckle-sharp-sdk, specklepy, speckle-viewer-webgpu, speckle-converters and speckle-server-internal. Header, units codes, primitive codes 0-12, flag bits 0-10, mesh body order (pad-to-8 before normals and uvs, none before colors), curve display-polyline-then-NURBS, whole-blob SHA-256 id, CRC over body only: all confirmed byte-for-byte in SgeoFormat.cs/SgeoEncoder.cs and sgeo.py. Facts corrected on the page during this pass: the geometries `type` column holds the lowercase primitive name (mesh, line, ...) for SGEO rows and the host label (3dm) for SOLID rows, not an 'encoding'; DEFINES ord is the definition's member ordinal (shared with DEFINES_MEMBER/DEFINES_INSTANCE), only DISPLAY/SOLID/CENTERLINE have per-object counters; nested polycurve/region segments sit behind an 8-byte prefix (u32 length + reserved u32); the .dat index has seven sections ending in realizations; the shard roll happens before a blob would exceed 1536 MiB. Nuance kept out of reader copy: the .dat builder is datgen, shipped in the speckle-converters image and orchestrated by the server as a job (speckle-converters/datgen/README.md); .NET SgeoEncoder/SgeoDecoder live in the Speckle.Sdk project under namespace Speckle.Objects.Utils.
